name: ViewfinderVR
summary: A head-following panel shows the user's view like a camera viewfinder; they freeze it, place and zoom it within reach, and then select distant objects by pointing at or touching their images on the panel.
howItWorks: With Quest hand tracking, the panel mirrors the view until the non-dominant hand pinches it, which freezes the image; the panel can then be moved and rotated, and middle- or ring-finger pinches with vertical hand motion zoom the view or resize the panel. Looking at the open palm resets it. Objects are selected through the panel either with a ray from the dominant hand plus a pinch (ViewfinderVR-Ray) or by pushing the index fingertip through the panel (ViewfinderVR-Touch). In an ISO 9241-9 Fitts task with 20 participants, Touch took 1.29 s at 3.16 bit/s and Ray 1.69 s, against 2.38 s and 1.64 bit/s for raycasting, with lower workload; setting up the panel took about 21 s. It does not help with occluded targets.
